children: Vection Technologies
is proposing to acquire US education technology business zSpace for approximately US$9.5 million in a predominantly share-funded transaction.
The Australian technology group also has plans for a simultaneous A$5m placement to support the acquisition, provide working capital, and fund integration and sales expansion.
The proposed combination would bring together Vection’s AI and extended reality (XR) products with zSpace’s customer network spanning more than 3,500 US school districts.
Completion remains conditional on financing, creditor arrangements, litigation outcomes, and other approvals, while the capital raising is not conditional on the acquisition proceeding.
Share-Based Consideration
Vection proposes to acquire all of zSpace through a cash-out merger, with approximately US$9.2m payable in Vection shares to principal creditors and sellers 3i, Fiza and Itria.
That consideration includes US$5.43m in shares at settlement and US$3.79m deferred across four quarterly tranches, with pricing floors and market-based adjustments.
Approximately US$0.3m in cash would be used to acquire the remaining public shareholding, while up to US$3.5m of further performance-based consideration may become payable.

The proposed A$5m placement is priced at 1.0575 cents a share, a 24.5% discount to the 15-day volume-weighted average price, with one attaching option for every two shares subject to shareholder approval.
Vection has separately outlined a secured bridge facility of up to US$5m for zSpace, with further drawdowns at its discretion and an initial US$350,000 advance.
Education Network Reach
zSpace supplies headset-free three-dimensional learning computers and curriculum content for science, technology, engineering and mathematics, and career-focused education.
Its installed footprint includes more than 20,000 Inspire units, while renewable software contracts had an annualised value of US$9.4m at 30 June 2026.
The business generated US$27.9m of revenue in calendar 2025, although revenue declined to US$10.6m in the first half of 2026 from US$14.2m a year earlier.
Vection recorded A$39.8m in revenue from contracts and A$6m in underlying EBITDA for the year ended June 2026.

Combining those results with zSpace’s latest 12-month revenue produces an illustrative A$74.5m revenue base, but the figures are unaudited, exclude acquisition accounting and do not constitute a forecast.
Turnaround Risks Remain
Vection intends to distribute its Algho AI tools and 3DFrame content through zSpace’s education channel, with a joint 21-product roadmap beginning in March 2027.
Management is targeting more than A$100m in combined annual revenue by 2028, an ambition dependent on improved zSpace trading, cost savings and cross-selling rather than contracted sales.
zSpace remained loss-making in the first half of 2026, with its financial statements identifying substantial doubt about its ability to continue operating.
The acquisition also depends on the outcome of litigation brought by EdtechX, scheduled for trial in January 2027, alongside the proposed restructuring of existing debt and other conditions.
If the acquisition does not proceed, Vection may redirect placement funds to alternative acquisitions or general working capital, while interim advances to zSpace carry recovery risk.

title: Vection Technologies Proposes zSpace Acquisition And $5m Placement
